Camila: quick heads up — int8 canary for kestrel-v2q is producing structured outputs that sometimes omit optional fields or reorder keys, which trips our strict funcall parser. sample below. @Raj @Marta :eyes:

Camila: ```
# example A (works)
{"action":"create_ticket","payload":{"title":"Login bug","priority":"high"}}
# example B (sometimes)
{"payload":{"title":"Login bug","priority":"high"},"action":"create_ticket"}
# parser treats ordering as non-canonical -> strict-parse fails
```

Raj: how big is the failure slice? numbers?

Camila: running canary across 2k requests. parse_fail_rate ~ 0.6% overall but concentrated on short prompts and some batching configs. retry succeeds ~70% of the time (we have soft-retry).

Marta: can we add a non-strict fallback that normalizes keys before schema validation? that seems cheaper than rolling back quant for now. also: we should audit our test set to include shuffled-key variants.

Theo: +1 on fuzzing the schema. I ran a quick mutation test yesterday (key-shuffle, optional-field-drop, array-permute) and saw similar flakiness on int8 on low-temp. I'll post the script. :thinking:

Theo: ```python
# tiny fuzz harness
from random import shuffle, choice
def shuffle_keys(obj):
  # naive: converts to list of pairs, shuffles, reserializes\  pairs = list(obj.items())
  shuffle(pairs)
  return dict(pairs)
```

Camila: started a targeted run with schema-fuzzing enabled + per-route telemetry. seeing parse_fail_rate jump to 1.4% on the routing path with small batch sizes (batch=1-4).

Marta: important note: our funcall contract expects exact key names and order for some legacy handlers (ugh). we need a compatibility shim in the toolrouter that does tolerant-parse -> canonicalize -> call. fallback should be opt-in per route.

Raj: do we have telemetry to show which keys are missing/reordered? that would guide a targeted shim rather than full lax parse.

Camila: yes — I pushed a sampled trace (5% sampling) to s3 and added a quick heatmap: common reorderings are action <-> payload, sometimes nested payload keys missing if quant truncation kicks in after tokenization. attaching link: https://redwood-internal/s3/canaries/1738372000/fuzz-traces (sample)

InfraBot: Canary run completed: kestrel-v2q-int8 2024-03-22T16:07:15Z. metrics: requests=2048, parse_fail_rate=1.4%, avg_latency_ms=42, retries_triggered=15, rollback_flag=false

Marta: next steps proposal: 1) add route-level tolerant-parse shim (opt-in) 2) add schema-fuzz tests to onboarding pipeline 3) adjust retry budget telemetry to split "parse-retry" vs "generator-retry" 4) consider PTQ tweak for short sequences if fuzzing shows strong correlation.

Camila: agree. I'll open a PR for the shim and a canary job to run schema-fuzz harness for new models. assigning the follow-ups: @Marta shim design, @Raj add telemetry split, @Theo extend fuzz harness to include tokenization truncation cases.

Raj: I'll instrument the retry metrics today. can we decide on acceptable parse_fail_rate threshold for canary? current hosted policy is 0.2% for strict schemas.

Marta: propose 0.3% for canary (with tolerant-shim allowed) but 0.1% for GA on strict routes. we should also surface per-route exceptions in console.

Camila: noted. I'll put together a short runbook for oncall: when parse_fail spikes -> enable route-shim -> run targeted fuzz-suite -> triage.

Theo: dropping the augmented fuzz harness link here: https://redwood-internal/ci/fuzz/kestrel-fuzz (contains mutation configs and tokenizer edge cases).

Camila: thanks all. I'll follow up with PRs and a short demo in tomorrow's sync. :thumbsup:
